challenges.name: review-checklist-statements
challenges.title: An automated review checklist: what it proves
challenges.description: Two statements about the automated checklist that runs on every CodeDev pull request: what a passing tests check tells you about PR #612, and which packages the dependency check reports for a package.json diff.

questions.explanation: False. The tests check only asks whether a test file changed when source files changed; src/courses/search.test.ts was added, so it passes. It cannot tell whether the test asserts anything useful, and this one passes for any function that returns an array - including the injectable query. A checklist turns cheap, mechanical questions into a red or green mark so the human reviewer can spend their time on the questions it cannot answer: does the test fail when the behaviour is wrong? The misconception is to read a passed check as a passed review.

True. zod only changed its version range, so it is not new. lodash moved from devDependencies to dependencies; it was already in the project, so it is not new either, even though it is not on the allowlist. sql-sanitize-lite is in neither section before and not on the allowlist, so it is the one finding - the package the agent invented in lesson 3.1, this time added to package.json. The rule targets the supply-chain question "what code is entering the project that nobody has vetted?"; version bumps and moves are reviewed differently (changelog, lock file diff). The misconception is that any change to package.json is a new dependency, which makes the check so noisy that people stop reading it.

challenges.name: automated-review-checklist
challenges.title: An automated review checklist for pull requests
challenges.description:
Before a human opens a pull request on the CodeDev API repository, a bot posts a checklist. Most PRs are now written with an AI assistant, and the same mechanical problems keep coming back: source changed with no test, a package nobody has vetted, a forgotten console.log, files the task never mentioned, and PRs too large to review. Write reviewChecklist(pr).

Input (JSON on stdin): { files: [{ path, status ("added" | "modified" | "removed" | "renamed", path is the new path), additions, deletions, addedLines: string[] }], packageJson: { before, after } (each may have dependencies and devDependencies: { name: version }, either may be missing), policy: { knownDependencies: string[], allowedPaths: string[], maxChangedLines } }.

Output: a JSON array of exactly five { check, passed, details } objects in this order. details is sorted (default string order) without duplicates, and passed is true exactly when details is empty.
1. "tests": a source file is a path that starts with "src/", ends with .ts, .tsx, .js or .jsx, does not end with .d.ts and is not a test file. A test file has ".test." or ".spec." in its file name, or a folder named test, tests or __tests__ in its path. Ignoring removed files: if at least one source file changed and no test file changed, details = those source paths.
2. "dependencies": every name in after (dependencies or devDependencies) that was in neither section of before and is not in knownDependencies.
3. "debug_markers": for every file that is not removed, "<path>: <marker>" for each marker TODO, FIXME and console.log( found in any of its addedLines (case-sensitive substring), once per file and marker.
4. "paths": every changed file, removed ones included, whose path matches no allowedPaths entry. An entry ending in "/" matches paths that start with it; any other entry matches only that exact path.
5. "size": the sum of additions + deletions of all files except lock files (file name package-lock.json, yarn.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml). If it is greater than maxChangedLines, details = ["<sum> changed lines, limit <maxChangedLines>"].
hints: Each check is a small function that returns a list of findings; passed only says whether the list is empty. Which files does each check look at - all of them, or only the ones that were not removed?

Write the two path predicates first (isTestFile and isSourceFile) and the allowedPaths matcher, and test them on src/courses/__tests__/search.ts, src/types/global.d.ts, srcx/tools/seed.ts and README.md.orig. For dependencies, build the set of names from both sections before and after, so a package that moved between sections is not new.

A similar check on a different input: report lessons whose slug changed but whose redirect list did not. findings = lessons.filter(l => l.slugChanged && !l.redirectAdded).map(l => l.id); then [...new Set(findings)].sort() and { check: "redirects", passed: findings.length === 0, details }. One small rule, one list, sorted and deduplicated at the end.
